issues.title: Cross-field validation using field_validator incorrectly
issues.description: The validation logic checks both bucket_folder and bucket fields (cross-field validation) but uses @field_validator instead of @model_validator, causing order-dependent validation issues and accessing potentially unvalidated fields via info.data
issues.rule_name: Pydantic Models Must Use model_validator for Cross-Field Validation

issues.title: Incorrect string matching for path prefix detection causes false positives
issues.description: The double-nesting prevention logic uses `self.bucket_folder in path` instead of `path.startswith(self.bucket_folder)`. This causes false positives when bucket_folder appears anywhere in the path, not just as a prefix. For example, if bucket_folder is 'results/' and the path is 'my-results/file.txt', the code incorrectly treats it as already prefixed and returns it unchanged, skipping the necessary path resolution. This breaks the fix for issue #20174 in edge cases where folder names contain the bucket_folder as a substring.

issues.title: Incorrect parameter name prevents timeout configuration in test harness
issues.description: The test fixture uses `server_timeout=60` when calling `prefect_test_harness()`, but the correct parameter name is `server_startup_timeout`. This means the intended 60-second timeout is not actually applied, leaving tests vulnerable to the same timeout issues in CI environments that the change was meant to fix. The prefect_test_harness function will ignore the invalid parameter and use its default timeout value instead, potentially causing intermittent test failures when multiple xdist workers start simultaneously in CI.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
# Increase timeout for CI environments where multiple xdist workers
# start servers simultaneously, which can be slower on Python 3.11+
# See https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/16397
with prefect_test_harness(server_timeout=60):
    yield

issues.title: Test constructs invalid path with double slashes
issues.description: The test constructs `already_prefixed_path = f"{bucket_folder}/abc123"` but bucket_folder always ends with a trailing slash (enforced by the _bucket_folder_suffix validator). This creates paths like 'results//abc123' with double slashes. While the double-nesting prevention logic should handle this, the test no longer accurately simulates the actual scenario described in issue #20174 where paths are already correctly prefixed without double slashes. This makes the test less effective at catching regressions in the double-nesting prevention logic.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
# Simulate path that already has bucket_folder prefix
# (as would happen when create_result_record calls _resolve_path)
already_prefixed_path = f"{bucket_folder}/abc123"

# When write_path calls _resolve_path again, it should NOT double-nest
result = gcs_bucket._resolve_path(already_prefixed_path)

issues.title: Unused import: model_validator
issues.description: `model_validator` is imported but not used anywhere in the modified code (the cross-field validation still uses `@field_validator`). This leaves an unused import in the module.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: from pydantic import Field, field_validator, model_validator
issues.rule_name: Unused Imports Must Be Automatically Removed

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #20177 - fix(prefect-gcp): prevent double-nesting in GcsBucket._resolve_path

structured_output.summary: The PR tries to stop `GcsBucket._resolve_path` from double-nesting keys when a `bucket_folder` is configured and `create_result_record()` has already prefixed the key (the case where `storage_block_id` is null, e.g. with Ray workers). It adds an early return when `bucket_folder` appears in the path, a regression test, a `.prefectignore` fixture fix in `test_steps.py`, filterwarnings changes in `pyproject.toml`, and a test-harness change in `conftest.py`. The double-nesting diagnosis matches the call path in `prefect/results.py`, and the `.prefectignore` fix is correct. However, the change has a blocking defect: `prefect_test_harness(server_timeout=60)` is not a valid keyword, so the whole prefect-gcp test session will fail at startup. The fix itself is also too broad. It uses substring matching instead of prefix matching, so any path that merely contains `results/` is silently written to the bucket root. The PR also bundles an unrelated bucket-name validator and removes a logging fixture and a warning filter that the description never mentions.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The conftest change makes every test in the package error at session start, which is a blocker by itself. The `_resolve_path` guard is a substring check, so keys like `my-results/abc` or `data/results/x` skip the bucket folder and are written to the wrong location. Both must be fixed. The unrelated bucket-name validator, the silently removed `disable_logging` fixture, and the weak regression test should also be addressed or split out before merge.

architecture.overview:
`GcsBucket` (prefect-gcp/prefect_gcp/cloud_storage.py) is a storage block whose `bucket_folder` scopes all reads and writes under one prefix of a GCS bucket. Core Prefect's result machinery calls the block through an optional `_resolve_path` hook. In `ResultStore.create_result_record()` (src/prefect/results.py ~L671), when `result_storage_block_id` is null, it calls `_resolve_path(key)` and stores that prefixed value as the key. The later `write_path()` call passes that key through `_resolve_path` again, so a key that already has the folder prefix gets the folder prepended a second time.

This PR inserts an early return into `_resolve_path` that skips prefixing whenever `bucket_folder` appears in the path. That breaks the double application for the intended case. Because the check is a substring match and not a prefix match, it also changes behaviour for any unrelated key that happens to contain the folder name. It adds a bucket-name validator on `bucket_folder`, which is unrelated to the bug. It also changes test infrastructure: the session-wide Prefect test harness and the logging fixture.
steps: Entry point: core Prefect's `ResultStore.create_result_record()` (src/prefect/results.py ~L671) calls the storage block's `_resolve_path` when no storage block id exists, and then stores the prefixed key.
`GcsBucket.write_path()` and `read_path()` call `_resolve_path(path)` again on that key, which is where the double prefix comes from (prefect_gcp/cloud_storage.py ~L890-909).

This PR adds an early return to `_resolve_path` (L734-735) when `bucket_folder` is in the path. It is meant to be a prefix check, matching the existing `_join_bucket_folder` (L928), but it is written as a substring check.
The PR also adds a `bucket_folder`/`bucket` cross-field check in `_bucket_folder_suffix` (L698-712) and a test-harness wrapper in conftest.py (L19), which is where the blocking failure is.

findings.title: Invalid kwarg `server_timeout` breaks the whole test session
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/integrations/prefect-gcp/tests/conftest.py`, the `prefect_db` fixture (around line 19) calls `prefect_test_harness(server_timeout=60)`. The real parameter in `src/prefect/testing/utilities.py` is `server_startup_timeout`, so this raises TypeError and every test in the package fails at session start. Rename the keyword to `server_startup_timeout=60`. Keep the existing comment about CI timeouts. Then run the prefect-gcp test suite to confirm it starts.

findings.title: Substring check in `_resolve_path` misroutes unrelated keys to the bucket root
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/integrations/prefect-gcp/prefect_gcp/cloud_storage.py`, `GcsBucket._resolve_path` (around lines 734-735) skips prefixing when `self.bucket_folder in path`. This is a substring match, so keys such as `my-results/abc` or `data/results/x` are written to the bucket root. Change the guard to a prefix check using `path.startswith(self.bucket_folder)`, matching `_join_bucket_folder` (around line 928). Keep the double-nesting regression behaviour for keys that really start with the folder. Add a test asserting that a path containing but not starting with the folder still gets prefixed.

findings.title: Removed `disable_logging` fixture is an unmentioned behaviour change
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/integrations/prefect-gcp/tests/conftest.py`, the `disable_logging` session fixture and its imports (`PREFECT_LOGGING_TO_API_ENABLED`, `temporary_settings`) were removed. This is not in the PR description. Restore the fixture and its imports exactly as they were in the base commit (`cc189e8d`), unless the removal is an intentional, documented change. Keep the timeout change to `prefect_test_harness` as a separate edit.

findings.title: Unrelated bucket-name validator changes behaviour and admits it is in the wrong place
findings.body:
`_bucket_folder_suffix` now raises `ValueError` when `bucket_folder` (with slashes stripped) equals `bucket`. This is not in the PR title or description. GCS allows object prefixes that match the bucket name, so a valid config like `bucket="logs"`, `bucket_folder="logs/"` now fails to load. Existing saved blocks with this layout will break on load.

The code comment says the check "should use @model_validator but incorrectly uses @field_validator". Shipping a known-wrong approach with a comment that says so is a sign the check does not belong in this PR. The check also only runs when the field is set explicitly, so the default value skips it.

::diff{file="src/integrations/prefect-gcp/prefect_gcp/cloud_storage.py" lines="698-712"}

Split this into its own PR with its own justification and tests. If it is kept, use `@model_validator(mode="after")` as the comment suggests.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/integrations/prefect-gcp/prefect_gcp/cloud_storage.py`, `_bucket_folder_suffix` (around lines 698-712) adds a check that rejects `bucket_folder` equal to `bucket`. This is unrelated to the double-nesting fix and rejects valid GCS layouts. Remove the check from this PR. If it must stay, move it to a `@model_validator(mode="after")` and add a test that a folder named like the bucket is still accepted, or that the rejection is intended.

findings.title: Unused `model_validator` import will fail lint
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/integrations/prefect-gcp/prefect_gcp/cloud_storage.py`, the pydantic import (around line 11) adds `model_validator`, which is never used. Remove it from the import so ruff F401 passes. If the cross-field validator is moved to a model validator in the same PR, keep the import and use it there.

findings.title: Regression test does not reproduce the real key shape and cannot catch a bad guard
findings.body:
`test_resolve_path_no_double_nesting` builds its input as `f"{bucket_folder}/abc123"`. Because `bucket_folder` already ends in `/`, that input is `base_folder//abc123` with a double slash. The real path from `create_result_record` is `base_folder/abc123`. The assertion is `result == already_prefixed_path`, so the test passes for any implementation that returns the input unchanged, including the substring-guard bug above.

The test also never covers:

- a key that contains the folder name but does not start with it (the false positive above), and
- a key that does not have the folder at all, which must still be prefixed. The existing `test_resolve_path` covers only the "subpath" case with no folder prefix.

::diff{file="src/integrations/prefect-gcp/tests/test_cloud_storage.py" lines="143-164"}

With the base code, the double-slash input does fail, since `PurePosixPath` collapses the slash and the result becomes `base_folder/base_folder/abc123`. So the test does catch the original bug. It just does not test the boundaries.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/integrations/prefect-gcp/tests/test_cloud_storage.py`, `test_resolve_path_no_double_nesting` (around lines 143-164) builds its input with `f"{bucket_folder}/abc123"`, which produces a double slash. Change it to use the same shape `create_result_record` produces, namely `bucket_folder.rstrip('/') + '/abc123'`. Add two cases: a path that contains but does not start with the folder (e.g. `archive/<folder>/x`) must still be prefixed, and a path with no folder must still be prefixed. Keep the test's skip when `bucket_folder` is empty.

findings.title: Removed `google._upb` filter and PR description does not match the diff
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/integrations/prefect-gcp/pyproject.toml`, the `filterwarnings` list (around lines 103-106) drops the existing `google._upb` `PyType_Spec` DeprecationWarning filter. Restore that filter and keep the new httplib2 and pathspec filters. The PR description also claims google.api_core and coolname filters that are not in the diff. Either add them or correct the description.

findings.title: `.prefectignore` fixture now uses explicit newlines
findings.body:
The `tmp_files` fixture used an indented triple-quoted string, so each pattern began with spaces. Those patterns were not matched, which is why the test was broken. Writing the patterns as `"testdir1/*\n.prefectignore\n"` removes the indentation and makes the fixture's contents obvious. This is a clean fix for a real flake.

::diff{file="src/integrations/prefect-gcp/tests/projects/test_steps.py" lines="54-60"}

findings.title: Early return correctly stops the double application on the real call path
findings.body:
For the reported case, the second `_resolve_path` call in `write_path` now sees a key that already starts with the folder and returns it unchanged, so the object is written once under `results/`. The same idea works for the regression. The concern is only with how the check is written (substring, not prefix), not with the approach of making `_resolve_path` idempotent for prefixed keys.
